Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Church life

repent verb

also repentance, be sorry for one’s sins

classical

Curt. 8.6.23 (Lewis & Short)
Plin. Ep. 7.10.3 (Lewis & Short)
Quint. 9.3.12 (Lewis & Short)
Vulg. Mt. 3.2

paenitentiam agere

Post-Augustan prose (Curtius, Pliny), and the Vulgate’s Poenitentiam agite, in the Clementine’s spelling. Repentance is paenitentia (Liv., Tac.).

Examples

  • Poenitentiam agite: appropinquāvit enim rēgnum caelōrum.

    Repent, for the kingdom of heaven is at hand.Vulg. Mt. 4.17

  • Imprūdēns peccat, quem post factī paenitet.

    He who is sorry afterwards did wrong without thinking.Publil. I 42

  • piget, pudēscit, paenitet

    we are vexed, ashamed and sorry (the morning’s regret)Prud. Cath. 2.26

Other words

  • paenitet, paenitēre, paenituit — repent of (impersonal)

    also used · classical · Publil. I 42; Vulg. Lc. 17.4

    Impersonal: mē peccātī paenitet, I repent of my sin, with the accusative of the person and the genitive of the thing (see I’m sorry).

See also sin, forgive, forgiveness, confession, I’m sorry.

SourcesLewis & Short: paenitentia · Lewis & Short: paeniteo

Vulgate verses checked against the Clementine Vulgate (CrossWire VulgClementine, via the scrollmapper bible_databases repository) and Hetzenauer’s edition, in Clementine spelling.
